text:
maria: paging — incident-bot just fired a P1 for canary fanout errors, high 5m error rate in eu & apac. seeing 503/502s from edge in eu-west-1. anyone oncall?
incident-bot: Pager triggered: canary_fanout_errors (threshold 5m) — severity P1. Links: /runbooks/canary-fanout, /dashboards/canary-errors.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout v2026.3 started at 2026-03-15T09:12Z: routes updated: eu=10%, apac=5%.
nashwin: tagging @oncall-eu — can you take triage?
oncall-eu: I'm on it, joining otoh. quick status: dashboards show a sharp spike in 502s around 09:16 UTC, correlated with an increase in queue wait times on eu infer cluster. taking logs now.
ben: logs from proxy show `upstream response code: 502`, upstream host pointing to `model-svc-v2026.3-abc` and `model-svc-v2026.2-def` in same ASG. looks like a partial image mix during canary rollout — kernel mismatch error in runtime. stack traces include `KVCacheInitError: incompatible-kernel`
caroline: ack. this matches the suspicion from preflight that the new kernel selection wasn't pinned properly for the canary image. i'm going to open the kill-switch for canary routing while we confirm impact.
maria: do it, we need to stop customer impact asap. what's the command?
caroline: running the emergency route flip:```bash
# set green to 100% for eu and apac, effectively disabling canary
infra route set-weight --service inference --region eu-west-1 --weight-green 100 --weight-blue 0 --commit "emergency kill-switch - canary kernel mismatch"
infra route set-weight --service inference --region apac-southeast-1 --weight-green 100 --weight-blue 0 --commit "emergency kill-switch - canary kernel mismatch"
```
deploy-bot: Route changes applied in eu-west-1 and apac-southeast-1. New traffic weights take effect; canary traffic drained.
oncall-eu: after flip, error rate dropped from 12% -> 0.9% in eu within 60s, p50 latency back to baseline. continuing to validate.
ben: capturing evidence for postmortem: container image digests showed mixed push timestamps; looks like a partial CI race ended up tagging two different images with the same tag for v2026.3 in eu pipeline.
nashwin: customer-facing: @support-bot and @maria, can we quantify impact? how many customers/requests failed?
support-bot: initial assessment: ~7 managed customers experienced increased error rates for ~4 minutes during ramp window; rough estimate 2.1k requests failed. no billing incidents reported. I'll open a customer-impact ticket and notify affected accounts.
maria: good. also notify SRE and Release Leads. caroline, do we want a rollback of the canary image tag from registry or just fix tagging and re-deploy canary?
caroline: immediate plan = keep kill-switch in place (stop canary traffic), revert any automation that re-tagged images, and hold full rollout. we'll prepare a fixed canary image with explicit digest and re-run canary later.
ben: adding that the kube daemonset had a cron that pulled images with `:latest-canary` float — we should deprecate floating tags for rollouts.
nashwin: oncall handoff: @ben will continue with infra cleanup, @caroline will own release fix, @maria will coordinate comms. we should page next-of-kin if rollback fails.
incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged by oncall-eu. Timeline will be recorded.
caroline: i've created a short mitigation PR to pin digests and blocked the release pipeline for v2026.3 in eu/apac gates. link: https://gh/redwood/repo/pull/4321
maria: thank you. follow-ups: postmortem, automation check on tagging, add an alert for mixed-image digests during rollouts, improve canary gating to validate kernel compatibility.
support-bot: sent initial customer notification to 7 accounts (templates applied). will prepare follow-up with technical notes once we have root cause.
ben: confirming cluster health now stable. will keep watch 15m.
oncall-eu: handing off monitoring to @ashwin for the next 2 hours. I'm marking this thread resolved for immediate mitigation; will re-open if errors re-occur.
maria: closing: mitigation applied, customer notifications sent, rollback not required at infra level because kill-switch routed traffic away. next: full postmortem and automation fix tracked in ENG-INC-789. :white_check_mark:
